answer: Anchor each agent to an amateur-radio callsign. First, the agent passes the radio exam and gets a unique callsign in a public registry. Second, it proves control by transmitting a signed challenge over the air, logged by three independent listening stations. Third, the network rejects any callsign already registered. Faking this costs an exam, a $300 radio, and a license tied to one real person, so a hundred fake agents need a hundred exams and radios. A sybil swarm is a reef of fake boats with no harbor to dock in, and a whisper on a real frequency is easy to hear and hard to fake.
